articles.title: Commission designates ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox under the Digital Services Act
articles.description: The European Commission has designated ChatGPT as a Very Large Online Search Engine, and Reddit and Roblox as Very Large Online Platforms under the Digital Services Act.
articles.content: The designations bring the services under additional DSA obligations intended to address systemic risks, including risks to minors, fundamental rights and public security. The Commission says the designations follow assessments of user numbers and the services’ role in the information environment; the obligations apply alongside other EU digital rules.

articles.title: At TechBBQ, Europe's AI conversations kept coming back to who's actually in control
articles.description: TechCrunch's coverage of Copenhagen's TechBBQ conference highlights a central European AI question: who controls the models, infrastructure and decisions shaping the region's AI future?
articles.content: The report captures investors, founders and operators debating control and agency as AI becomes embedded in products, companies and public life. For Europe, that discussion connects technical capability with dependence on foreign platforms, governance choices and the practical question of who remains accountable when AI systems act.

The seed funding will deepen the product and expand partnerships with hearing clinics and related healthcare organisations in Europe and North America.

articles.title: Paris-based Hugging Face launches $399 open-source Microduck robot
articles.description: Hugging Face and Bordeaux subsidiary Pollen Robotics unveiled Microduck, a $399 open-source robot that developers can train with reinforcement learning.
articles.content: The 25-centimetre robot can walk, pick up objects with its beak, recover from falls and even roller-skate. It ships with camera, lidar and motion sensors, and its SDK and training stack are open source. Pre-orders topped $2.6 million in the first 24 hours. The product continues Hugging Face's push from models into physical AI after acquiring Pollen Robotics.

articles.description: PitchBook data reported by Handelsblatt show German startups raised EUR9.36 billion from January to July 2026, already above the 2022 full-year pace, led by AI, robotics and defence firms.

articles.description: Warsaw is considering fast-track legislation and has already pledged compute offtake as it competes for a mid-sized EU AI Gigafactory.
articles.content: Poland signed the EuroHPC joint procurement agreement and adopted a resolution guaranteeing access, with an initial national commitment of more than PLN 400 million to buy compute. Public support for a Polish site could reach EUR1 billion. Officials describe a mid-scale facility of at least 75,000 AI accelerators. Demand from member states already exceeds the seven sites the EU programme envisages.

articles.title: Spain is the only EU bidder putting the state in control of an AI Gigafactory consortium
articles.description: SETT, Spain's public digital-transformation company, holds 47.99% of the consortium bidding for an EU AI Gigafactory, plus a 1% Catalan government stake.
articles.content: El Economista reports that Germany, France, Italy, Portugal and Poland are backing bids with public money or offtake commitments but have not taken controlling equity. Spain's structure makes the state the largest shareholder. France has pledged about EUR100 million as a compute customer rather than an owner. The contrast highlights different national approaches to EU compute sovereignty.

articles.title: Itoflow raises 1.8m pounds to build AI agents for investment teams
articles.description: UK startup Itoflow closed a $2.5m (1.8m pounds) pre-seed led by Balderton Capital to turn each firm's research process into governed AI agent workflows.
articles.content: Founded in 2026, Itoflow builds agents that learn how professional investors research opportunities, manage risk and review portfolios across equities, bonds, ETFs, commodities and digital assets. The platform aims to encode a firm's own philosophy rather than impose one. Capital will expand engineering and quantitative research and support commercial and regulatory work. Angels include Cleo founder Barney Hussey-Yeo.

articles.title: AI takes 60% of European venture value in H1 2026
articles.description: PitchBook-based analysis finds AI absorbed 60.3% of European deal value in the first half of 2026 as funding concentrated in fewer, larger rounds.
articles.content: European startups raised EUR44.1 billion across just over 1,740 deals in H1 2026. State-backed and pan-European funds dominate deal count, led by the EIC Fund, Antler and High-Tech Gruenderfonds. Defence AI is a valuation outlier: Munich's Helsing closed $1.8 billion at an $18 billion valuation in July. The piece maps who is writing the cheques behind Europe's AI concentration.

articles.title: France's H1 2026 tech ledger is led by AI labs AMI and Mistral
articles.description: Tech.eu's H1 2026 ranking shows France still among Europe's top funding markets, with Yann LeCun's Advanced Machine Intelligence raising a $1 billion seed and Mistral adding $830 million.
articles.content: Besides Eutelsat's EUR975 million debt deal, AMI's world-model lab and Mistral's model-plus-infrastructure raise dominated the list. AMI, founded by LeCun and Alexandre LeBrun, plans teams in Paris as well as New York, Montreal and Singapore. Mistral is expanding from models into agents and training infrastructure for businesses and governments. The figures underline Paris's weight in European foundation-model capital even as compute and talent stay scarce.

articles.title: UK startup Callosum raises $100 million seed to run AI across mixed chips and models
articles.description: Cambridge-founded Callosum closed a $100 million seed led by Atomico to build software that runs AI workloads across heterogeneous chips and models.
articles.content: Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI programme also participated. Callosum argues that real-world problems need mixed models and hardware rather than a single model on identical GPUs. The company has partnered with Cerebras and previously raised $10.25 million when it left stealth. The round is one of Europe's largest AI seed financings of 2026.

articles.description: Copenhagen-based Velatir closed a EUR5 million seed co-led by Spintop Ventures and Ugly Duckling Ventures to expand its Europe-hosted AI management layer.
articles.content: Velatir helps organisations govern growing internal AI use. The platform runs on European-owned and hosted infrastructure rather than US hyperscalers, a pitch built around data sovereignty. EIFO provided a matching loan; Norrsken Evolve and angels including n8n's Jan Oberhauser participated. Funds will expand the team and European sales six months after pre-seed and commercial launch.

articles.title: CEPR analysis: AI Act transparency applies while high-risk rules slip to 2027-28
articles.description: A VoxEU column argues that the Digital Omnibus left Europe in a double bind: Article 50 transparency took effect on 2 August 2026, but standalone high-risk obligations move to December 2027.
articles.content: Regulation 2026/1744 deferred Annex III high-risk rules by 16 months and product-embedded high-risk AI to August 2028. What remains in force is the duty to tell people when they interact with AI and to mark synthetic media. The authors say the delay preserves some competitiveness but weakens the EU's claim to set the first fully operational high-risk AI regime.

articles.title: AI Act enforcement begins as Brussels sets out who polices GPAI and transparency
articles.description: The Brussels Times reports that from 2 August 2026 the Commission's AI Office and national authorities enforce GPAI rules, transparency duties and prohibited practices.
articles.content: The AI Office can request documentation, evaluate models and fine providers of general-purpose AI, including systemic-risk models. National authorities handle other systems; the European Data Protection Supervisor oversees EU institutions. Professor Alessandro Abate of Oxford was appointed Lead Scientific Adviser, supported by a 60-expert Scientific Panel. The Omnibus delays standalone high-risk rules to 2 December 2027 and product-embedded high-risk AI to 2 August 2028. New bans on non-consensual intimate imagery and CSAM apply from 2 December 2026.

articles.title: Commission starts enforcing AI Act rules and transparency duties from 2 August
articles.description: The AI Office and national authorities began enforcing the AI Act on 2 August 2026, including rules that require certain systems to disclose AI interaction and mark AI-generated content.
articles.content: From 2 August 2026 the European Commission's AI Office can enforce rules for general-purpose AI model providers, while national authorities enforce other applicable obligations. Chatbots and interactive systems must tell users they are dealing with AI. Deepfakes must be labelled and synthetic content must carry machine-readable marks. High-risk system rules remain deferred by the AI Omnibus to December 2027 and August 2028. More than 180 organisations have signed the Code of Practice on transparency of AI-generated content.

articles.title: EU opens call for up to seven AI Gigafactories to unlock more than EUR30 billion
articles.description: EuroHPC and the Commission launched a tender for up to seven industry-led AI Gigafactories, backed by up to EUR10 billion in public funds and aiming for at least EUR20 billion in private investment.
articles.content: The facilities will combine advanced AI processors, software, cloud stacks, connectivity and energy-efficient data centres for training, inference and fine-tuning frontier models. Eighteen Member States signed the joint procurement agreement. The call closes on 12 November 2026, with selections expected in early 2027 and operations within 18 months. The Commission also signed letters of intent with AMD, NVIDIA and Qualcomm on hardware access.

articles.title: Commission publishes Article 50 guidelines on AI transparency duties
articles.description: On 20 July 2026 the Commission issued guidelines explaining which providers and deployers must disclose AI interactions and label synthetic content from 2 August.
articles.content: The guidelines interpret Article 50 of the AI Act. Providers must design systems so users know they are interacting with AI and add machine-readable marks to generated or manipulated content. Deployers must inform people about deepfakes, unreviewed AI text on public-interest matters, and emotion-recognition or biometric-categorisation systems. The guidelines sit alongside the Code of Practice on marking and labelling AI-generated content.
